description.en: How FundsXML evolves and how to take part: who decides about the standard, the FundsXML Standards Committee and the three working groups (Content & Technique, Promotion, Documentation), associate and full membership, contributing on GitHub, the path of a change request from proposal to a new version, small and large changes, and what makes a good change request.

say.en: How does FundsXML evolve, and how can you take part? In this film you see who decides about the standard, which working groups there are, how to join them, how a change request becomes part of a new version, and what makes a good change request.

items.head: The standard follows its users
items.text: It changes when the people who use it ask for it.

items.head: Regulation changes every year
items.text: New templates, new instruments, new fields.

items.head: Every change affects many partners
items.text: Hear about it early, plan your systems.

items.head: Your requirements, your timing
items.text: Bring them in before the decision is made.

say.en: Why should you take part at all? Because the standard follows the people who use it. Regulation changes every year, new templates appear, and markets bring new instruments. Every change to FundsXML affects many partners at once. Whoever takes part brings in their own requirements early, hears about changes before they arrive, and can plan their own systems accordingly.

FundsXML belongs to no single company. It is run by FundsXML dot org, a not-for-profit organisation of the fund industry. Its rules are set out in a charter. At the top stands the FundsXML Standards Committee. A secretariat organises the work, working groups do the work on the standard, and members and the wider community bring in their needs.

items.head: Fund companies and associations
items.text: Members from AT, DE, DK, FR, LU, NL and CH.

items.head: Meets at least twice a year
Sets up the working groups
items.text: And names their chairs.

items.head: Decides on members and releases
items.text: When results become a new version.

say.en: The Standards Committee, or F S C, is the governing body. Its members are fund companies, service providers and fund associations from several European countries. It meets at least twice a year. It decides on new members, it sets up the working groups and names their chairs, and it decides when the results of a working group become a new version of the standard.

items.head: Content & Technique
items.text: Maintains the schema, designs new structures, keeps the standard consistent.

items.head: Promotion
items.text: Makes FundsXML known across Europe, talks to new members and partners.

items.head: Documentation
items.text: Guides, examples and references for implementers, including these films.

say.en: The work itself happens in three working groups. Content and Technique is the technical heart: it maintains the schema, designs new data structures and keeps the standard consistent. Promotion makes FundsXML known across Europe and talks to new members and partners. And Documentation creates the guides, examples and references that help users implement the standard, including films like this one.

items.head: Associate member
items.text: Free, apply on fundsxml.org.

items.head: Join a working group
items.text: Form on fundsxml.org/about.

items.head: Contribute on GitHub
items.text: github.com/fundsxml

say.en: There are three ways in. First, become an associate member. It is free, any company or person can apply on the website, and members receive the news and invitations of FundsXML. Second, join a working group: on the About page of fundsxml dot org, a short form asks for your name, your e-mail and the group you are interested in. Third, contribute on GitHub, where the schema, the examples and the tools are public.

items.head: Full members
items.text: Fund companies, asset managers, associations. Admitted by the committee, with a vote.

items.head: Associate members
items.text: Free, open to everyone. More than 110 companies today.

items.head: Both
items.text: Invited to the working groups. An annual meeting for associate members.

say.en: Full membership is meant for fund companies, asset managers and national fund associations. The Standards Committee decides on it, and full members have a vote. More than a hundred and ten companies support FundsXML as associate members today. Both kinds of members are invited to take part in the working groups, and at least once a year there is a meeting for the associate members.

On GitHub, the organisation fundsxml publishes the schema, the example files, and also these videos. In the schema repository you can follow every change: issues describe problems and wishes, pull requests contain proposed changes, and the changelog lists what each version brings. Anyone can read along, and anyone can open an issue.

en.headline: Anyone can propose a change.
en.sub: A new field, a new code, a correction, or a whole new area.

say.en: The most direct way to shape the standard is a change request. Anyone can submit one: a member, a software provider or a single user. A change request may be a new data field, a new code value, a correction, or a whole new area, such as a new regulatory template.

en.title: The path of a change request

items.head: Proposal
items.text: To a working group or committee member, or as a GitHub issue.

items.head: Working group
items.text: Decides on a working draft.

items.head: Working draft
items.text: Structure and examples.

items.head: Review
items.text: By the committee, or in public.

items.head: New version
items.text: With a changelog entry.

say.en: This is the path of a change request. It is submitted in writing to the working group or to a member of the Standards Committee, or as an issue on GitHub. The working group decides whether it goes into a working draft. The draft is reviewed. And when it is approved, it becomes part of the next version of the schema, with an entry in the changelog.

items.head: Small change
items.text: New optional fields, corrections. The working group decides; the committee has 5 working days to object.

items.head: Large change
items.text: Structure or compatibility changes. Committee vote and public comment of at least 20 days.

say.en: How long the review takes depends on the size of the change. Small changes, such as new optional fields or corrections that keep existing files valid, are decided by the working group, and the committee has five working days to object. Large changes, which alter the structure or break compatibility, need a vote of the committee and a public comment period of at least twenty days.

items.head: Today
items.text: A document carries its size, but no checksum.

items.head: The problem
items.text: A receiver cannot verify an embedded file.

items.head: The proposal
items.text: An optional element Checksum with the algorithm, e.g. SHA-256.

items.head: Small change
items.text: Optional, so existing files stay valid.

say.en: An example. Today a document in FundsXML carries its size, but no checksum, so a receiver cannot be sure that an embedded file arrived unchanged. A change request could propose an optional checksum element with the algorithm, for example S H A two five six. Since it is optional and keeps existing files valid, it would count as a small change.

en.title: The change request as an issue
en.code:
Title: Add an optional checksum to Document

Use case
  Receivers of embedded KIDs want to verify that the file
  arrived unchanged.

Proposal
  New optional element after SizeInBytes:

  <SizeInBytes>18734</SizeInBytes>
  <Checksum algorithm="SHA-256">9f2c…e41a</Checksum>

Compatibility
  Optional: existing files stay valid (small change).

say.en: Here is how such a request could look as an issue. A short title. The use case: receivers of embedded key information documents want to verify them. The proposal: an element Checksum after the size, with the value and an attribute for the algorithm. A small XML example. And the note that the element is optional, so existing files stay valid.

items.head: The business case
items.text: Who needs the data, and why.

items.head: The data point
items.text: Meaning, type, codes.

say.en: What makes a good change request? Describe the business case: who needs the data, and why. Define the data point exactly: its meaning, its type and its codes. Add a short example in XML. Say whether existing files stay valid. And name the partners who would use it. A clear request saves the working group a lot of time.

That was how to take part in FundsXML: the committee, the working groups, membership and change requests. You find the contact form on fundsxml dot org, and the schema on GitHub. The next series shows FundsXML in a real file, for developers. Thanks for watching.
